title: OTE Calculator (With Pay Mix and Quota-to-OTE Ratio)
summary: Free OTE calculator. Enter base pay, target variable pay, and quota to see the pay mix, pay at 50%, 100%, and 150% of quota, and the quota-to-OTE ratio.
body_markdown:
Two sales jobs can offer the same on-target earnings (OTE) and still leave reps with different paychecks. Say both jobs have a $200,000 OTE. The first pays $160,000 of it as base pay and $40,000 as variable pay. The second splits it evenly, with $100,000 of each. If each rep sells half of quota, they get their full base pay plus half of their variable pay. The first rep earns $180,000, and the second earns $150,000.


The OTE calculator below shows how much of a rep's pay package is guaranteed and how much depends on hitting quota. Enter a rep's base pay, target variable pay, and quota. You'll see the rep's OTE, the pay mix, what the rep earns at three levels of quota, and how the quota compares with the pay.


Sales leaders can use it to check that a quota is fair for the pay before the package goes into an offer letter. Reps weighing a job offer can see how much they'd earn if they fall short of quota.


Below the calculator, we break down a $200K OTE package and show the typical pay mix for four sales roles. You'll also learn what a fair quota-to-OTE ratio looks like and what to ask before you accept an OTE offer.


If you're looking to work out the commission on specific deals, use the[Sales Commission Calculator](https://www.captivateiq.com/explainer/sales-commission-calculator) .

This calculator assumes pay grows in a straight line with sales, with no cap and no accelerators. Real plans often have both, so actual pay can be higher or lower.


How this is calculated


` OTE = base pay + target variable pay`


` pay mix = base pay ÷ OTE / target variable pay ÷ OTE`


` pay at X% of quota = base pay + (target variable pay × X%)`


` quota-to-OTE ratio = quota ÷ OTE`


` commission rate = target variable pay ÷ quota`


Variable pay grows at the same rate for every dollar sold. A rep at 50% of quota earns half of the target variable pay, and a rep at 150% earns one and a half times it. The base doesn't change.


The 4.6x median comes from The Bridge Group's 2026 report on account executive pay and quotas. A ratio within 0.3 of the median shows as close to it.


## How to Use the OTE Calculator


Enter three numbers for one rep, each for a full year:


- **Base pay:** The salary the rep gets whether or not they hit quota
- **Target variable pay:** The commission or bonus the rep earns at 100% of quota
- **Yearly quota:** The amount the rep is asked to sell in a year
‍


As you fill it in, the calculator updates six results:


Result What it shows


OTE What the rep earns in a year at 100% of quota


Pay mix How OTE splits between base pay and variable pay


Pay at 50%, 100%, and 150% of quota What the rep earns for selling half of quota, all of it, or one and a half times it


Monthly pay The base paid each month, and the average monthly pay at 100% of quota


Commission rate Target variable pay ÷ quota, the rate a plan needs to pay OTE at quota


Quota-to-OTE ratio How many dollars the rep sells for each $1 of OTE, next to the 2026 median of 4.6x


The calculator assumes pay grows in a straight line with sales. A rep who sells half of quota earns half of the target variable pay. Caps and accelerators bend that line, but the calculator leaves them out because every plan sets them differently.


[Accelerators raise the commission rate](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/sales-compensation-accelerators) after a rep passes quota.[A cap stops variable pay](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/uncapped-commissions) at a set amount, no matter how much more the rep sells. Plans often have both, so actual pay can be higher or lower than the calculator shows.


## What Is OTE?


OTE, short for on-target earnings, is the total pay a rep earns in a year if they hit 100% of quota. Target variable pay is the commission or bonus a rep earns for hitting exactly 100% of quota. To get OTE, add base pay and target variable pay:


**OTE = base pay + target variable pay**


Our[full guide to on-target earnings](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/on-target-earnings-in-sales) covers how companies set OTE for each role.


## What Does $200K OTE Mean?


On a 50/50 pay mix, a $200K OTE is a $100,000 base plus $100,000 of target variable pay. The calculator above starts with the same numbers. At 50%, 100%, and 150% of quota, here’s what the rep earns:


Share of quota hit Variable pay Total pay for the year Average pay per month


50% $50,000 $150,000 $12,500


100% $100,000 $200,000 $16,667


150% $150,000 $250,000 $20,833


Of the $200,000 OTE, only the $100,000 base pay is guaranteed. Paid over 12 months, the base pay comes to $8,333 a month ($100,000 ÷ 12) whether the rep closes one deal or none. On a plan with accelerators, the rep in this example would earn more than $250,000 at 150% of quota.


We use $200,000 because it was the[median OTE for account executives](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/research/2026-ae-models-motions-metrics) (AEs) in 2026. It was $190,000 in 2024 and $167,000 in 2022, so typical AE pay at quota grew about 20% in four years.


## What Is Pay Mix?


Pay mix is how OTE is split between base pay and variable pay. It's written as two percentages with base pay first, like 70/30.


A 70/30 pay mix means 70% of OTE is base pay and 30% is variable pay. On a $100,000 OTE, a 70/30 mix is a $70,000 base and $30,000 of target variable pay. The larger the second number, the more of the rep's pay depends on hitting quota.


Role What the role does Typical pay mix (base/variable) Source


Sales development rep (SDR) Books meetings for AEs 68/32[The Bridge Group, 2025](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/research/2025-sdr-models-metrics-report-the-bridge-group)


Account executive (AE) Finds new customers and closes deals 53/47[The Bridge Group, 2024](https://blog.bridgegroupinc.com/2024-ae-metrics-compensation-benchmark)


Account manager Grows accounts the company already has 59/41[WorldatWork survey, 2022](https://worldatwork.org/media/CDN/dist/CDN2/documents/pdf/resources/research/WorldatWork_RSCH_Sales-Comp-Programs-and-Practices_2022.pdf)


First-line sales manager Leads a team of reps, with no accounts of their own 66/34[WorldatWork survey, 2022](https://worldatwork.org/media/CDN/dist/CDN2/documents/pdf/resources/research/WorldatWork_RSCH_Sales-Comp-Programs-and-Practices_2022.pdf)


A 50/50 split is the most common pay mix in[CaptivateIQ's 2025 sales compensation benchmarks](https://www.captivateiq.com/resources/captivateiq-2025-sales-compensation-benchmarks-report) . Roles with[more influence over the buying decision](https://www.alexandergroup.com/insights/sales-compensation-the-perplexing-topic-explained/) usually get a bigger variable share. AEs have the most influence over whether a new customer buys. Their variable share is the biggest of the four roles, at 47%. SDRs don't close deals. First-line sales managers don't have accounts of their own. Both roles get about two-thirds of their pay as base.


## What Is a Good Quota-to-OTE Ratio?


The[median quota-to-OTE ratio for account executives](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/research/2026-ae-models-motions-metrics) was 4.6x in 2026, up from 4.2x in 2024. On a $200,000 OTE, a 4.2x ratio means an $840,000 quota. At 4.6x, it's $920,000, so the typical rep now sells $80,000 more for the same pay.


To find the ratio, divide quota by OTE. A ratio of 5x means the rep has to sell $5 for every $1 of OTE. The calculator's default rep has a $1 million quota and a $200,000 OTE. Divide $1 million by $200,000, and you get 5.0x, a little above the 4.6x median.


When the ratio is far above 4.6x, the quota is high compared with the pay. The rep has to sell more than the typical AE to earn the same OTE and may have a hard time hitting quota.


If the ratio is far below 4.6x, the pay is high compared with the quota. Each dollar of sales costs the company more in pay than it does at the typical company.


Close to the median, the rep has a fair chance to earn OTE at a normal cost to the company. It's important that companies give reps a fair chance because[less than half of AEs hit quota](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/research/2026-ae-models-motions-metrics) in 2026 (48%, down from 51% in 2024). A rep who misses quota earns less than their OTE. Companies that set quotas too high lose reps to jobs where OTE is within reach, and replacing them means paying to hire and train someone new.


If your quota is far from 4.6x, use the[Sales Quota Calculator](https://www.captivateiq.com/explainer/sales-quota-calculator) to set quota from your revenue target and hiring plan.


## Questions to Ask Before You Accept an OTE Offer


The OTE in a job offer is what the job pays at 100% of quota. Ask these four questions to find out how likely you are to earn it.


1. **What share of the team hit quota last year?** If only a few reps did, the OTE is harder to reach than it looks. Compare the answer with 48%, the share of AEs who hit quota in 2026. If the team is well below that, plan on earning less than your OTE.
2. **Is there a cap, and are there accelerators?** A cap limits what you can earn above 100% of quota. Accelerators pay a higher rate on every dollar you sell past quota. Together they tell you how much more than your OTE you can earn in a strong year.
3. **How long is the ramp?** Ramp is the time a new rep needs to reach full speed. New AEs took an average of 6.2 months to fully ramp in 2026,[the longest The Bridge Group has recorded](https://www.bridgegroupinc.com/research/2026-ae-models-motions-metrics) . Ask whether your quota is lower or part of your variable pay is guaranteed during those months.
4. **When is commission paid?** Some plans pay commission when a deal closes. Others pay when the customer pays the invoice, sometimes months later. Knowing which one helps you plan your budget, especially in your first few months, when most of your pay is base.


Once you have answers, enter the offer's base pay, target variable pay, and quota in the calculator above. Look at what you'd earn at half of quota. If you could live on that number in a slow year, the offer is safer than its OTE alone suggests.


## OTE Calculator FAQs


### Is OTE guaranteed?


No. Only base pay is guaranteed. The variable part of OTE depends on how much of quota the rep sells. A rep with a $200,000 OTE on a 50/50 mix is guaranteed $100,000.


### How do you calculate OTE?


Calculate OTE by adding base pay and target variable pay. A $60,000 base plus $40,000 of target variable pay is a $100,000 OTE, with a 60/40 pay mix.


### What is a good pay mix for sales reps?


A good pay mix matches the role. AEs, who close new deals, had a median mix of 53/47 in 2024. SDRs, who set up meetings but don't close, had a median mix of 68/32 in 2025. Account managers and first-line sales managers get more of their pay as base than AEs do, because their results depend more on existing customers and on their team than on deals they close themselves.
